# MSBuild Code Review — `StyleIssues.sln`

## Solution Structure

| Path | Type |
|---|---|
| `Directory.Build.props` | Root shared properties |
| `Directory.Build.targets` | Root shared targets |
| `LibA/LibA.csproj` | C# class library |

| `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` | F# executable |

---

## 🔴 Errors (will cause incorrect builds or subtle bugs)

### 🔴 E1 — `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `.props` is dead code (AP-21)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, lines 10–12

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (all projects in this repo), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation — it is only set inside the SDK `.targets` import, which runs *after* `Directory.Build.props`. This condition **never** matches, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is silently never set. Multi-targeting projects would work, but only by accident (the outer dispatch sets it as a global property).

**Fix:** Move this block to `Directory.Build.targets`:

```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E2 — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 13–15

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Two bugs here:**

1. **Overwrite instead of append.** This replaces all prior constants (`DEBUG`, `TRACE` from the SDK). Code guarded with `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop compiling.

2. **Unquoted condition.** `$(Configuration) == Debug` should be `'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'`. Without quotes, if `Configuration` is empty or contains spaces, MSBuild will throw a parse error or produce unexpected results.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
  <DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E3 — Property defaults in `Directory.Build.targets` silently override project settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–11

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `Directory.Build.targets` is imported **after** the project file. Any unconditional property assignment here wins over what the project file sets. In `LibB/LibB.csproj` line 13, the project explicitly sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>`, but this `.targets` file overwrites it back to `true`. The project-level opt-out is dead code.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` where they serve as overridable defaults (projects import `.props` before their own content):

```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

If you truly need `.targets`-level enforcement for `TreatWarningsAsErrors` but still want opt-out, use a conditional default:
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E4 — Publish-on-build target forks a second project instance (bin/obj race)
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** The `<MSBuild>` task re-invokes the same project with an additional global property (`_IsPublishing=true`). This creates a **second project instance** in the build graph. Both instances share the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, so they race writing `obj/` and `bin/` files, causing intermittent build failures — especially under parallel builds (`-m`).

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish in the *same* project instance:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);PublishAfterBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="PublishAfterBuild" DependsOnTargets="Publish"
        Condition="'$(DesignTimeBuild)' != 'true'" />
```

Or, if you need publish-on-build, use the built-in SDK property:
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <PublishAfterBuild>true</PublishAfterBuild>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E5 — `SetTargetFramework` on single-targeting ProjectReference causes double build
**File:** `LibB/LibB.csproj`, line 24

```xml
<ProjectReference Include="..\LibA\LibA.csproj" SetTargetFramework="TargetFramework=net8.0" />
```

**Problem:** `LibA` is single-targeting (`net8.0`). `SetTargetFramework` injects `TargetFramework=net8.0` as a global property, creating a *different* project instance (`LibA + {TargetFramework=net8.0}`) from the one the solution already builds (`LibA + {}`). Both instances write to the same `bin/obj` paths, racing on file writes. `SetTargetFramework` is only appropriate when referencing a multi-targeting project to pin a specific TFM.

**Fix:** Remove the `SetTargetFramework` attribute:
```xml
<ProjectReference Include="..\LibA\LibA.csproj" />
```

---

### 🔴 E6 — Legacy assembly reference instead of PackageReference
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 27–30

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a `packages.config`-style raw assembly reference in an SDK-style project. The `HintPath` points to a `packages\` folder that won't exist in a clean clone/restore — the build will fail with a missing reference. Additionally, it targets `net6.0` assets while the project targets `net8.0`, which is a TFM mismatch.

**Fix:** Replace with a `PackageReference`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E7 — F# file ordering bug causes compilation failure
**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** In F#, **file order is significant** — files can only reference types defined in files listed *above* them. `Services.fs` is listed before `Domain.fs`, but services almost certainly depend on domain types. This will cause `FS0039` (value/type not defined) errors. Compare with the working `OrderService.fsproj` which has the correct order: `Domain.fs` → `Services.fs` → `Program.fs`.

**Fix:**
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns, not immediately broken but problematic)

### 🟡 W1 — Hardcoded Windows-only `OutputPath`
**Files:** `LibA/LibA.csproj` line 7, `LibB/LibB.csproj` line 7

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

**Problem:** These are absolute Windows paths. On Linux/macOS (including CI), the build will write to a relative path `C:\builds\output\LibA` under the repo root (MSBuild doesn't fail, but creates a nonsensical directory tree). Developers' local builds will also conflict if they don't have `C:\builds\` set up.

**Fix:** Use relative paths or `$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)`:
```xml

### 🟡 W2 — Analyzer package leaks to downstream consumers
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, lines 16–18

<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```
